metadata.name: Peptic ulcer disease (gastric/duodenal)
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but bleeding and perforation are emergencies
metadata.severity: From mild dyspepsia to life-threatening haemorrhage/perforation

overview.short_description: A break in the stomach or duodenal mucosa (ulcer), usually caused by Helicobacter pylori or NSAIDs, presenting with epigastric pain and at risk of bleeding or perforation.
overview.detailed_description: Peptic ulcer disease is a common cause of dyspepsia and upper GI bleeding. Duodenal ulcers classically cause pain relieved by food/at night; gastric ulcers may worsen with food. The two dominant causes are H. pylori and NSAIDs. Diagnosis (when investigated) is endoscopic; treatment is acid suppression plus removing the cause (eradicate H. pylori, stop NSAIDs). Complications - bleeding and perforation - are emergencies, and gastric ulcers require follow-up to exclude malignancy.
overview.pathophysiology: Imbalance between mucosal aggressive factors (acid/pepsin, H. pylori, NSAID injury) and defence (mucus/bicarbonate, prostaglandins) leads to mucosal breakdown and ulceration; deep ulcers can erode vessels (bleed) or the wall (perforate).
overview.etiology: Helicobacter pylori and NSAIDs/aspirin dominate; also smoking, severe stress (critical illness), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (rare gastrin excess), and malignancy (gastric ulcers).
overview.natural_history: Heals with acid suppression and removing the cause; recurs if H. pylori persists or NSAIDs continue.
overview.prognosis: Good with treatment; complications increase morbidity/mortality, especially in the elderly on NSAIDs/anticoagulants.

prevalence.value: Common; lifetime risk is significant, though declining with H. pylori treatment and safer NSAID use.

incidence.value: Related to H. pylori prevalence and NSAID use.

mortality.value: Low uncomplicated; significant with bleeding/perforation, especially elderly.

epidemiology.age_groups: Any age; complications more common/serious in the elderly.

risk_factors.smoking: Impairs healing; increases risk and recurrence.
risk_factors.travel: H. pylori acquisition in endemic areas.
risk_factors.family_history: H. pylori clustering; family history of gastric cancer.
risk_factors.medications: NSAIDs/aspirin (major), corticosteroids and anticoagulants/antiplatelets (bleeding), SSRIs, bisphosphonates.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Prior peptic ulcer/H. pylori; critical illness (stress ulcers).

chief_complaints.complaint: Pain relieved by food or antacids / night pain (duodenal)

chief_complaints.importance: Associated features; bleeding is a red flag

symptoms.symptom: Rhythmic pattern (duodenal: relieved by food/at night; gastric: worse with food)
Sudden severe epigastric pain with rigidity (perforation)

history_questions.question: Where is the pain and is it relieved by food/antacids or worse at night?
history_questions.why_ask: Rhythmic pattern suggests ulcer and location

history_questions.question: Any vomiting blood or black tarry stools?
Any weight loss, dysphagia, persistent vomiting, or family history of gastric cancer?
Prior ulcer or H. pylori infection?

physical_examination.examination: Assess for bleeding/anaemia and haemodynamic status

laboratory_tests.indication: All with peptic ulcer (test and eradicate)

laboratory_tests.expected_result: Anaemia with chronic loss; acute drop with haemorrhage

ecg.when_needed: If epigastric pain could be cardiac
ecg.findings: Used to help exclude cardiac cause.

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Upper GI endoscopy diagnoses ulcers, allows biopsy (H. pylori; gastric ulcers biopsied to exclude malignancy), and enables haemostasis for bleeding ulcers; repeat endoscopy to confirm gastric ulcer healing.
other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Biopsy of gastric ulcers (exclude malignancy) and for H. pylori

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Endoscopic demonstration of a mucosal ulcer (break) in the stomach or duodenum. Clinically suspected in dyspepsia (especially rhythmic pain, NSAID use, or bleeding). Always establish the cause (H. pylori/NSAIDs) and biopsy gastric ulcers to exclude malignancy.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: Risk scores (e.g., Glasgow-Blatchford/Rockall) assess upper GI bleeding severity.

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is there an ulcer on endoscopy or normal mucosa?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Alarm features; malignant ulcer on biopsy
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any weight loss or trouble swallowing?
Does the pain go to the back or is it right-sided after fatty food?
Is it brought on by exertion?

diagnostic_questions.question: Any vomiting blood, black tarry stools, or sudden severe abdominal pain with a rigid tummy?
Do you take NSAIDs/aspirin, and is H. pylori present?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Positive -> stop NSAIDs / eradicate H. pylori

next_best_question.question: Any bleeding/perforation features, NSAID use, alarm features, and H. pylori status?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Bleeding/perforation -> emergency; alarm features -> urgent endoscopy; otherwise -> PPI + H. pylori test-and-treat, stop NSAIDs

next_best_test.why: Diagnose/treat ulcer and biopsy gastric ulcers

red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - resuscitate, risk-score, urgent endoscopy; withhold/adjust anticoagulants per protocol

red_flags.finding: Sudden severe epigastric pain with a rigid, peritonitic abdomen (perforation)
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency surgical assessment (erect CXR/CT for free air)
Biopsy and repeat endoscopy to confirm healing (exclude malignancy)

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Upper GI bleeding and perforation (emergency); alarm features (urgent endoscopy).
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Non-healing/recurrent ulcers, refractory disease, or suspected rare cause (e.g., Zollinger-Ellison).

initial_management.supportive_care: Assess for bleeding/perforation; explain the cause and treatment.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Proton-pump inhibitor; H. pylori eradication regimen; NSAID/aspirin review. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG184, ACG_HPYLORI_2024.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Stop smoking, reduce alcohol; avoid NSAIDs; take essential aspirin with gastroprotection.
initial_management.follow_up: Confirm H. pylori eradication where indicated; repeat endoscopy for gastric ulcers to confirm healing and exclude cancer.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Proton-pump inhibitor to heal the ulcer (typically weeks); H. pylori eradication if positive (and confirm eradication); STOP NSAIDs/aspirin where possible or add long-term gastroprotection if essential. For bleeding ulcers: resuscitation, endoscopic haemostasis, IV PPI.

patient_education.home_advice: A peptic ulcer is a sore in the stomach or the first part of the gut, usually from a bacterium (H. pylori) or anti-inflammatory painkillers. Acid-reducing tablets heal it, and treating the cause (antibiotics for H. pylori, stopping NSAIDs) prevents it coming back. This is serious if it bleeds or bursts: get emergency help if you vomit blood, pass black tarry stools, or have sudden severe tummy pain.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: القرحة الهضمية جرح في المعدة أو بداية الأمعاء، غالباً من جرثومة (الملوية البوابية) أو مسكّنات مضادة للالتهاب. تُشفيها أدوية تقليل الحمض، وعلاج السبب (مضادات حيوية للجرثومة وإيقاف NSAIDs) يمنع عودتها. تصبح خطيرة إذا نزفت أو انثقبت: اطلب المساعدة الطارئة إذا تقيّأت دماً، أو نزل براز أسود قطراني، أو حدث ألم بطن مفاجئ شديد.
patient_education.prevention: Avoid unnecessary NSAIDs (gastroprotection if essential), eradicate H. pylori, stop smoking, limit alcohol.
patient_education.warning_signs: Vomiting blood, black tarry stools, sudden severe abdominal pain, weight loss, or difficulty swallowing.

evidence.evidence_level: High for PPI healing and H. pylori eradication; strong for endoscopic management of bleeding.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_CG184, ACG_HPYLORI_2024; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Heal the ulcer, eradicate H. pylori, remove ulcerogenic exposure and prevent/refer bleeding.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Proton-pump inhibitor; H. pylori eradication regimen; NSAID/aspirin review. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_CG184, ACG_HPYLORI_2024.

non_drug_measures: Smoking cessation and avoidance of unnecessary NSAIDs; confirm eradication after therapy.

medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

monitoring: response and ongoing indication; magnesium/B12/iron or bone risk when clinically indicated
